message:
Axial length fits the box with room for the brake. Plain words: the spinning nose plus the body plus a finger of air at the back take less than four hand widths, so all moving parts stay inside. The stack sum of 8 cm overhang plus 25 cm nacelle plus 3 cm clearance (E52) is 36 cm against the 45 cm cube, leaving 9 cm margin for Safety-Control Integrator's disc in the side-view shutdown layout (E50).

Brake rails carry the stop twist into the post without rubbing. Plain words: the little clamp that grabs the disc tries to twist the body, and two small rails under it feed that twist straight into the stiff post so the shaft cannot shift into the blades. I confirm what Safety-Control Integrator takes from Braking ideas for wind turbines (E42) that spring-applied pads press a disc, which from my side means the caliper reaction must go through the bedplate rails in the nacelle bedplate sketch with brake rails (E58) to the post clamp; the survival thrust (E22) of 37.3 N is a heavy shopping bag, the bending stress (E27) of 16.6 Megapascal (MPa), meaning million newtons per square metre, is about 16 times below the 276 MPa typical yield in the Aluminum 6061-T6 — Material Datasheet (E55) and the 5/12/23, 3:58 PM ASM Material Data Sheet Aluminum 6061-T6; 6061-T651 (E56), with tip bend (E26) 0.516 mm against 25.0 mm side gap.

Parked hold does not yet stay parked, so Aero-Rotor Lead must prove stall relief. Plain words: the wind trying to turn the stopped rotor at full storm is stronger than the pad holding it, and the stop heat itself is harmless like a warm cup. Required hold with factor 1.5 (E54) is 0.720 N·m against the 0.400 N·m pad in the spring disc (C21) and the 0.480 N·m storm aero torque in the electrical-only runaway check (E48), which I raise as blocking objection to the spring disc (C21) in O1; the disc temperature rise from spin energy (E53) is 4.35 K, meaning degrees of warming, so Power-Systems Engineer and Safety-Control Integrator can enlarge the pad radius or Aero-Rotor Lead can show soft stall drops storm torque below 0.400 N·m.

Not ready, because the parked-hold mismatch in O1 plus axial bench proof still needs Manager decision.
